interpretation: Instruction: 'Pick the akita black bowl on the cookie box and place it on the plate'. Robot: capx_libero_panda (7-DoF Panda, parallel-jaw gripper, max width 0.079 m, closed_empty 0.985, held_below 0.95; cameras agentview (scene) and robot0_eye_in_hand (wrist); control_dt 0.05 s, 7990 steps). At the start, perception showed the target bowl as obj13 (grey/black patterned bowl, rim centre about (0.745, 0.028), rim radius about 0.054 m, rim top z about 0.057), sitting on the cookie box. Only the box's front edge was visible, as obj14 (brown/red, top z about 0.008). The plate was obj9 (white with red rings, centre about (0.728, 0.208), radius about 0.068, rim top z 0.008, centre surface z about -0.004). The other black bowl, obj5 near (0.46, 0.18) next to a ramekin, is not the target because it is not on the cookie box. Goal state: that bowl resting on the plate, upright, ideally centred. Nothing ambiguous beyond which bowl is meant; the cookie box clearly identifies it.
plan: Initial plan: a top-down rim pinch on the bowl's +y side (toward the plate, away from the cabinet), fingers closing along y. I kept the home finger yaw of -90 deg because a yaw-0 orientation needed a 24 s wrist rotation. Then lift, carry so that the bowl centre is over the plate centre, lower, release and retract. The first grasp lost the bowl during the lift: the vertical pads touched the flared wall (about 25 deg from vertical) at only two points. The bowl fell off the box and ended up tilted about 30 deg between the box and the plate. I then made a mistake: I descended for a re-grasp with the gripper still closed. The closed fingers pressed on the high rim and rotated the bowl almost upright (about 12 deg tilt, -y side resting on the box edge). Revised plan: a pinch at the high -y rim with the gripper tilted about the world x axis (+13 deg), so the pads lay parallel to the wall and gave a flat pinch. After lifting, I measured the held bowl's rim plane from its gold edge and found it sits upright in the grip at a gripper tilt of about 14 deg. I carried it at that tilt, checked its rim centre against the plate centre (within 2 mm), lowered it to about 4 mm above the plate, released and retracted straight up.

steps.what: Read the embodiment, instruction and budget; listed objects; showed agentview, wrist and an object close-up; fitted the rim circle from obj13 points
steps.why: Identify the bowl on the cookie box and the plate, and get the bowl geometry
steps.result: Bowl obj13 on box obj14, plate obj9. Rim centre about (0.744, 0.027), r about 0.053, rim top z 0.056. Step 0.

steps.what: Tried a yaw-0 top-down move above the bowl, then compared finger yaws
steps.result: Yaw 0 needed at least 24 s (wrist rotation); yaw -90 (current) needed about 13.7 s. Kept yaw -90, fingers closing along world y.

steps.what: Moved the TCP above the bowl to (0.70, 0.027, 0.24) in 16 s; refit the rim from wrist-camera depth with the gripper's own points (z > 0.08) excluded
steps.why: Overhead view of the full rim and the inner wall profile
steps.result: Steps 0 to 326. Rim centre (0.7449, 0.0279), r 0.054, top z 0.057; inner radius 0.045 at z 0.045, 0.040 at z 0.034; inner bottom z 0.013.

steps.what: Pre-grasp above the +y rim (z 0.13), then descended to z 0.075; projected the planned finger spots into both cameras
steps.why: Verify the fingers straddle the rim before descending
steps.result: Steps 452 to 518. Overlays showed the inner finger over the bowl interior and the outer finger outside it.

steps.what: Descended to TCP (0.7445, 0.0775, 0.042) with a vertical top-down pose and closed the gripper
steps.result: Step 604. Reading 0.898 (8.2 mm gap), so something was held.

Step 680. FAILED: reading 0.9876 (closed_empty). The bowl slipped out and fell off the box, ending tilted about 30 deg (opening toward +y) between the box and the plate; perception merged it with the plate.

steps.what: Re-perceived; fitted the tilted bowl's rim plane from gold-edge points; took heightmap and cross-sections from the wrist depth
steps.why: Find the bowl pose for a re-grasp
steps.result: Rim normal (0.02, 0.51, 0.86), tilt 30.6 deg; high rim on the -y side at (0.75, 0.0495, 0.072) with a nearly vertical wall below it.

steps.what: Descended toward the high rim at (0.750, 0.0495, 0.057), not noticing that the gripper was still closed from the failed grasp
steps.why: Re-grasp (mistake: I did not reopen the gripper)
steps.result: Step 796. The TCP stopped 4.5 mm high, so the guard did not close. The closed fingers pressed the rim down, the bowl rotated nearly upright (about 12 deg tilt, -y side on the box edge), and the box tipped up briefly, then lay flat again.

steps.what: Lifted 6 cm, opened the gripper, re-measured the bowl from overhead depth
steps.why: Recover a clean state and get the new bowl pose
steps.result: Step 862. Rim centre about (0.749, 0.103); rim z 0.054 on the -y side and about 0.032 on the +y side (tilt about 12 deg toward +y).

steps.what: Planned and executed a pinch at the high -y rim, TCP (0.749, 0.0532, 0.0404), with the gripper tilted +13 deg about world x so the pads were parallel to the wall; closed the gripper
steps.why: A flat pinch resists the bowl's weight and torque better than the earlier two-point contact
steps.result: Pose reached within 0.4 mm (step 988). After closing at step 1018 the reading was 0.9334 (5.3 mm gap = wall thickness).

steps.what: Lifted 3 cm and checked; then lifted to z 0.12 and rotated to 25 deg
steps.why: Verify the hold, then try to bring the bowl upright
steps.result: Steps 1064 and 1180. Reading steady at about 0.93 and the bowl visibly in the air. The rim-plane fit on the segmented held bowl showed it tilted 10.9 deg the other way, so it is upright in the grip at about 14 deg.

steps.what: Carried the bowl at a 14 deg tilt to TCP (0.726, 0.159, 0.08) over 10 s (a 7 s version was refused as too fast); re-segmented the held bowl
steps.why: Put the bowl centre over the plate centre (0.7282, 0.2084)
steps.result: Step 1386. Held bowl rim tilt 1.2 deg; rim centre (0.7263, 0.2080), within 2 mm of the plate centre.

steps.what: Lowered to TCP z 0.038 (+2 mm x correction), opened the gripper, retracted 14 cm straight up in 5 s (a 3.5 s version was refused)
steps.why: Set the bowl down about 4 mm above the plate surface and release it without disturbing it
steps.result: Steps 1452, 1472 and 1578. The bowl stayed upright on the plate after release.

steps.what: Final check from agentview, the wrist camera and 3D views; rim-plane and plate-ring fits; finish_episode
steps.result: Bowl rim centre (0.7276, 0.2054) against plate ring centre (0.729, 0.208); tilt 2.3 deg; rim z about 0.046, consistent with the bowl resting on the plate. Finished at step 1578 of 7990.

key_images.caption: Start: target bowl obj13 on the cookie box (obj14 edge), plate obj9 to its right (+y)
First plan: vertical rim pinch on the +y rim; fitted rim (yellow) and finger spots projected into the wrist camera
First grasp failed on lift: the bowl slipped out and fell tilted between the cookie box and the plate
Mistake: descending with the gripper still closed pressed the high rim and rotated the bowl almost upright
Re-grasp plan: pinch at the high -y rim with the gripper tilted 13 deg so the pads lie along the wall
Flat pinch closed on the bowl wall (reading 0.933, 5.3 mm gap)
Bowl lifted and held securely under the tilted gripper
Held bowl upright (rim tilt 1.2 deg), its centre within 2 mm of the plate centre before lowering
Released on the plate: bowl upright and centred
Final state after retract: the bowl from the cookie box rests upright and centred on the plate

diagnosis: I believe the task succeeded, with nothing left to fix. Two side effects are worth noting. (1) The cookie box ended up lying flat but displaced by about 1 cm from where it started; it is not part of the goal. (2) The route there included a failed grasp (the bowl slipped during the first lift) and a careless re-grasp descent with the gripper still closed, which shoved the bowl. Both were recovered from, but on a less forgiving scene either could have knocked the bowl off the table or broken something. If a checker required more than 'bowl resting on the plate', residual risk is low: the final tilt is 2.3 deg and the centre offset is about 3 mm.
lessons: A vertical top-down pinch on a flared bowl rim (wall about 25 deg from vertical) touches the wall at only two points (inner finger low, outer finger high) and lost the bowl on lift. Tilting the gripper about the horizontal axis normal to the closing axis, so the approach runs along the wall and the pads lie flat on it, gave a pinch that held through lift, rotation and transport.
After any failed grasp, check robot.gripper_cmd and open the gripper before descending again; a closed gripper descending onto a rim pushes the object.
Gate the gripper close on the reached TCP pose (a few mm tolerance): it caught the bad descent here and avoided closing on top of the rim.

Measure the held object after lifting (segment it from a scene-camera pixel and fit the rim plane from its coloured rim edge). The bowl's orientation in the grip was not what the pre-grasp model predicted; correcting the gripper tilt from that measurement made it go down upright and centred.
When a tilted bowl merges with a neighbouring object in perception, depth heightmaps and cross-sections (and gold-rim colour points) give its pose reliably.

On this robot, previews quote min_duration; moves of 10-25 cm need several seconds, and wrist yaw changes are very slow. Use about 1.3x min_duration and keep the finger yaw near home when the task allows.
